'''Johann Jakob Rebstein''' (1840–1907) was a Swiss mathematician and [[surveyor]].

==Early life==
Rebstein was born on 4 May 1840 in [[Töss]], [[Switzerland]], to his father, a baker and his mother, a doctor.<ref name="eminger">{{cite web|last1=Eminger|first1=Stefanie Ursula|title=Carl Friedrich Geiser and Ferdinand Rudio : the men behind the first International Congress of Mathematicians|url=https://research-repository.st-andrews.ac.uk/handle/10023/6536|website=St Andrews Research Repository|hdl=10023/6536|access-date=31 May 2017}}</ref>{{rp|131}}

==Education and career==
Rebstein attended post-secondary school in [[Winterthur]], and after graduating in 1860, went on to study for a year at [[Collège de France]].<ref name="eminger"/>{{rp|131}}  He was professor of mathematics and physics in [[Zürich]] from 1877 to 1898.<ref name="mac">{{cite web|title=Johann Jakob Rebstein|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Rebstein.html|website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]|access-date=31 May 2017}}</ref> He was awarded his doctorate in 1895 from the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] for his work ''Bestimmung aller reellen Minimalflächen, die eine Schaar ebener Curven enthalten, denen auf der Gauss'schen Kugel die Meridiane entsprechen''.{{Efn|English: Determining All Real Minimal Surfaces That Contain a Family of Planar Curves, Which Correspond to the Meridians on the Gaussian Sphere<ref name="mac"/>}}<ref name="mac"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Jacob Rebstein|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=65927|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project|access-date=31 May 2017}}</ref> He is best known for his work in surveying, and for introducing the [[Traverse (surveying)|traverse]] method in Switzerland. Throughout his career, Rebstein was appointed as surveying expert for a number of [[Cantons of Switzerland|cantons]], including [[Thurgau]] (1863–1881), [[St. Gallen]] (1881–1894), Zürich (1886–1892), and [[Luzern]] (1894–1907).<ref name="mac"/>{{rp|131}}

In 1868 he was elected to the [[Swiss Concordat of Geometers]], and served as its president from 1887 until his death in 1907.<ref name="eminger"/>{{rp|132}}

In 1905 he was awarded an [[honorary doctorate]] from the [[University of Zürich]], for "outstanding contributions to actuarial sciences".<ref name="mac"/>

Rebstein was a member of the organizing committee for the first meeting of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref name="eminger"/>{{rp|79}}

==Death==
Rebstein suffered from [[kidney disease]] for the last several years of his life, and died in 1907 in Zürich.<ref name="eminger"/>{{rp|133}}

==Publications==
Rebstein's publications included:<ref name="eminger"/>{{rp|132}}
* ''Lehrbuch über praktische Geometrie mit besonderer Berücksichtigung der Theodolitmessung'' (1868)
* ''Die Kartographie der Schweiz, dargestellt in ihrer historischen Entwicklung'' (1883)
* ''Mitteilungen über die Stadtvermessung von Zürich1'' (1892)
